name: Variable-Length Coding
definition: A compression technique where the brick size is reduced by storing the minimum value as a base value and storing the difference from the base for each voxel. The number of bits per voxel (n) is determined by the brick's value range.
summary: Variable-Length Coding is a lossless compression technique that reduces storage by encoding voxel differences relative to a base value, offering finer granularity than fixed-width methods.
